chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Isma'il ibn Abd al-Khaliq, who said:

I heard him say: 'It is not appropriate for the Imam to rise [from bowing or prostration] when praying until everyone behind him has completed what was missed of the prayer.' And it is upon the Imam to make his recitation audible to those behind him.

key_terms.إِلْإِمَامِ: The leader of the congregational prayer

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for the Imam's movements and recitation during congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the Imam’s duty to maintain synchronization with followers by delaying his movements until they complete their actions, a ruling derived from the principle of *muqaddamah* (precedence) in prayer. Additionally, it mandates audible recitation (*jahr*) to ensure the congregation remains engaged and united in worship. These guidelines reflect the Shia emphasis on order and communal cohesion during Salah, as detailed in classical fiqh discussions on the qualities of the Imam.
